overview: Ireland is a popular destination for international students looking to study a undergraduate degree in business and management. In Ireland, a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) or other business degree can assist students in establishing a foundation in management, marketing, accounting, finance, entrepreneurship and international business.

items: There are a number of professional and academic benefits to studying business in Ireland.
International business environment: Ireland is home to a large number of multinational companies in the technology, financial services, consulting, pharmaceuticals and other sectors.
- Practical business education: Depending on the program, students can complete case studies, group projects, presentations, research assignments and business simulations.
- Multiple specialisations: Students can explore management, marketing, finance, accounting, international business, entrepreneurship and business information systems.
Global exposure: Students will work with people from different backgrounds and develop communication, teamwork and cross-cultural skills.
- Progression to postgraduate study: Graduates can apply for master’s degrees in business, management, finance, marketing or related subjects, provided they meet the relevant entry requirements.
Career development: A business degree can prepare students for entry-level positions in *business operations, sales, marketing, administration and financial services.
- English language learning environment: Students can learn and improve their professional communication skills in a English-speaking country
With the help of Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance students may explore these opportunities and know the eligibility for studying abroad.

BBA is typically a undergraduate business administration degree that introduces students to the main functions of an organization. In Ireland similar programs are often run under different qualification titles.
Some of the popular business degree choices in Ireland include:
Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA)

A BBA typically covers management, accounting, marketing, business strategy, economics, human resources and organizational behaviour where offered. Students should verify the precise award title and recognition of any program advertised as a BBA.
Bachelor of Commerce

A typical undergraduate Irish qualification is the Bachelor of Business . It may cover business management, marketing, accounting, finance, entrepreneurship and business operations. Some programs allow students to pick a specialization as they go.
Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com.)

Typically, a Bachelor of Commerce will include studies in commerce, economics, accounting, finance, marketing and management. This may be an option for students interested in corporate careers or advanced study in business.
Global Business

International Business programs focus on global markets, international strategy, cross-cultural management, trade and business expansion. Some courses include language study or opportunities for international study.
Accounting & Finance

The degrees concentrate on financial reporting, accounting principles, auditing, taxation, corporate finance and financial analysis. Students with an interest in pursuing a career in professional accounting should check whether the course offers exemptions or recognition from the relevant professional bodies.
Marketing & Entrepreneurship
These programs focus on customer behavior, branding, market research, digital marketing, business development and starting or growing a business.

sections.title: 4. Eligibility to Study BBA in Ireland

items: Students typically apply for a undergraduate business degree in Ireland after finishing their secondary education to a standard equivalent to Irish school-leaving qualifications.
General eligibility requirements are:
Educational qualifications
Class 12 or its equivalent school leaving qualification is normally required of applicants. Universities will compare international qualifications with their own entry standards.
Marks (Minimum)

Each university, course and applicant category has different required grades. Students should check the entry requirements for their specific board and qualification and not assume that one percentage requirement applies to all Irish institutions.
Course requirements

Many general business degrees are available to students from a variety of academic backgrounds. But some courses may have math and subject-specific prerequisites. Students should check the requirements for accounting, finance, economics and other programs with a quantitative focus.
Proficiency in English language
International students may be required to submit IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or other accepted English language test. The minimum scores vary by university and program.
For students in India

Those with CBSE, CISCE or state-board qualifications should refer to the university’s country-specific entry requirements. Entry is subject to standard qualifications, grades, subject requirements and English language requirements. Even if you meet the minimum requirements, that doesn’t mean you’ll be selected.
Students should check the official admission requirements for the selected business programme before application.
Typical documents that are requested are:
Class 10 and Class 12 certificates (or equivalent school-leaving certificates).
Mark sheets and academic transcripts.
A valid passport.
Results of English language tests (if necessary).
Personal statement or statement of purpose, if applicable.
Letters of academic reference or recommendation if required.
Relevant extracurricular activities or accomplishments, if requested.
Certified translations of documents not in English, if necessary.
Further documentation requested by the university.

Students applying through a centralized admissions system or directly to an institution should follow instructions for their applicant category . International applicants may follow different procedures to Irish and EU school leavers.

Cost of living
Cost of living in Ireland varies according to the city, accommodation and personal spending habits. Rents in Dublin can be very high. Students should plan for:
*Accommodation and utilities.
- Groceries and food.
*Public transport.
*Mobile phone or Internet.
- Medical insurance.
- Books and study material.
- Leisure and personal costs.
Other expenses
International applicants should also take into account costs associated with travel, visa, immigration registration and initial accommodation.
Scholarships and financial assistance
Some Irish Universities provide scholarships or merit based awards to eligible international students. Availability and value depend on institution, program, nationality and academic performance.

sections.title: 8. BBA Accreditation and Recognition in Ireland

items: Students should check that the institution and the qualification are accredited and are suitable to their academic or career goals before enrolling.
Important points to check are:
- Recognition of the awarding institution: Check that the institution is authorized to award the qualification.
- National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ): Most Irish honors bachelor’s degrees are at Level 8 and ordinary bachelor’s degrees are usually at Level 7. The level will depend on the program.
- Professional Recognition: Accounting, finance, and other professions may have particular requirements. Verify that the degree is recognized or exempted by the relevant professional body.
- International recognition: If you intend to study or work overseas, you should check how the qualification is regarded by the relevant employers, universities or professional bodies.
- Programme-specific details: Accreditation may be for a specific course or department, not necessarily for every program run by the institution.

A BBA and an Irish Bachelor of Business or Bachelor of Commerce may have common subjects but award titles and qualification structures can differ. Look at the official course specs, then make your decision.

sections.title: 9. BBA Jobs and Salary in Ireland

items: With a business degree in Irelandgraduates can apply for entry-level positions across a range of industries. Outcomes for employment are affected by specialization, practical skills, internships, communication abilities, employer requirements and work authorization.
BBA Career Opportunities
The possible roles are:
Business Development Executive
Marketing Assistant/Marketing Executive
Sales Executive.
Assistant Human Resources.
Operations co-ordinator
Accountant Assistant.
Customer Success Partner.
Business Support Officer.
Business Analyst – Junior
Recruiting Coordinator.
Project/Administrative Coordinator.
Management Trainee.

Graduates may also progress to further study such as a master’s degree in management, finance, marketing, international business or business analytics provided they satisfy the entry requirements of the program.
Salary after BBA
There is no specific average salary for BBA graduates in Ireland. Salary depends on the position, the employer, the location and the experience that applies.

As a rough guide you might expect to see entry-level business, sales, marketing and administrative positions paying €28,000–€40,000 gross per year. Your salary in an analytical, finance-related or specialist position will depend on your technical skills and the needs of the employer. These are rough estimates and not verified average salaries of BBA graduates.

faqs.q: Q2. What is the cost of studying BBA in Ireland?
faqs.a: The tuition fees for a BBA in Ireland vary depending on the university and the course. Examples of published fees for international students in 2026/27 are €9,000 per year at Galway Business School for its Bachelor of Business, €13,500 at TU Dublin for its Bachelor of Business (Honours), €17,000 at DCU for Business Studies International and €21,700 at UCC for its BComm (Hons). Additional living expenses and other charges.

faqs.q: Q3. What are the eligibility requirements for BBA in Ireland?
faqs.a: You’ll usually need a recognized Class 12 or equivalent qualification, with the required grades and any specific subjects. International students may also be required to show English-language proficiency . Specific criteria vary by institution and course.

faqs.q: Q4. What are the job opportunities after BBA in Ireland?
faqs.a: Graduates can apply for entry-level roles in business development, marketing, sales, operations, human resources, accounting support, customer success and administration. Career options will depend on your degree specialization, practical skills and relevant experience.
